title: Ground Handling Bulletin GHB-26-14: Winter De-icing and Anti-icing Operations

headings.text: Ground Handling Bulletin GHB-26-14: Winter De-icing and Anti-icing Operations

key_sentences: This bulletin sets out the procedures that all stations and contracted handling agents must follow when aircraft are de-iced or anti-iced during the 2026–27 winter season.
It replaces the previous bulletin in full and must be read together with the Ground Operations Manual, chapter 9.
Holdover time is the estimated period during which the anti-icing fluid prevents frost, ice or snow from forming on the treated surfaces.
The table below is reproduced for training purposes; in operation, always use the current holdover-time guidelines issued for the season.
Holdover time begins at the start of the final application of fluid, not at its end.
Before the aircraft leaves the de-icing pad, the de-icing lead must pass the anti-icing code to the commander by radio or by ACARS.
Messages sent by ACARS must follow the format below exactly.
The commander confirms receipt by repeating the fluid type and the start time.
Any fluid spill, equipment failure or missed holdover time must be reported through the safety reporting system before the end of the shift.
Stations send a weekly summary of de-icing movements to Ground Operations every Monday.

rows: All stations; ATR 72-600 and Dash 8-400 fleets

list_items.text: • The station manager ensures that only trained and authorised staff apply fluids.
• The de-icing lead decides the treatment method and records the start time of the final step.
• The commander remains responsible for deciding whether the aircraft is fit to take off.
Contamination check carried out on wings, tail and control surfaces
Fluid type and concentration confirmed against the batch sheet
Start time of the final step recorded
Anti-icing code passed to the commander
Post-treatment check signed by the de-icing lead
